row.basis: heavy hands; two supporters
row.note: Moses' hands become heavy, and Aaron and Hur hold them up from opposite sides; this is the commentary's concrete image of a failing body steadied by people on both sides.

row.basis: helpless travelers cry for help
row.note: The wilderness wanderers cry to the LORD in distress and are delivered; it supplies a narrative form for the move from a stranded traveler to nasta'inu, asking for aid.

row.basis: led by a straight way
row.note: After their cry, God leads the wanderers by a straight way to a settled place; it closely joins requested help to ihdina and the straight route.

row.basis: q-w-m B002; arise and hold a hand
row.note: Genesis tells Hagar to arise (Hebrew qumi) and to hold the boy's hand in the wilderness; the genuine q-w-m cognate joins the source's uprightness to hand-held aid.

row.basis: q-w-m B002; journey too much
row.note: The angel tells exhausted Elijah to arise and eat because the journey is too much for him; Hebrew qum gives the source's q-w-m standing image a traveler-specific setting of divine provision.

row.basis: strength to continue walking
row.note: Strengthened by the food, Elijah travels forty days to Horeb; this realizes the commentary's sequence in which help restores a body for the road.

row.basis: power for the faint
row.note: God gives power to the faint and strength to the powerless, directly matching the source's weak traveler who cannot proceed unaided.

row.basis: renewed strength; walk without fainting
row.note: Those who wait for the LORD receive renewed strength and walk without fainting; it gives the commentary's aided and composed walking an explicit divine outcome.

row.basis: upholding the stumbling; feeble knees
row.note: The speaker's words uphold one who stumbles and make weak knees firm; this supplies a verbal and social analogue to the bodily support in the commentary.

row.basis: feet for the lame
row.note: Job says he was feet to the lame; the figure makes another person capable of movement, as the source's helpers make a weak walker mobile.

row.basis: holding the right hand; divine help
row.note: God takes Israel's right hand and says, I help you; it fuses the commentary's hand-supported traveler with its explicit request for help.

row.basis: strengthen, help, uphold
row.note: God promises to strengthen, help, and uphold with the righteous right hand; the three actions closely mirror aid becoming upright stability.

row.basis: upholding falling; raising bowed
row.note: The LORD supports all who fall and raises those bowed down; it gives a divine counterpart to the source's movement from collapse toward an upright body.

row.basis: fall; hand held
row.note: Though the righteous fall, they are not cast down because the LORD holds their hand; the text makes support at the moment of failed footing the reason for recovery.

row.basis: hands bear up a foot
row.note: Angels bear the faithful person on their hands lest a foot strike a stone; it is a particularly close scriptural image for support that protects a traveler's gait.

row.basis: help from the LORD
row.note: The pilgrim identifies the LORD as the source of help; beside nasta'inu it makes aid a prayerful reliance rather than merely an abstract resource.

row.basis: foot not allowed to slip
row.note: The helper will not let the pilgrim's foot slip; it makes the aid of the preceding verse legible in the commentary's terms of stable walking.

row.basis: everlasting arms underneath
row.note: God's everlasting arms are beneath Israel; this gives the source's image of being borne from the sides a protective, sustaining underside.

row.basis: strengthen weak hands and knees
row.note: The prophetic command to strengthen weak hands and make feeble knees firm directly shares the commentary's debilitated body before it can walk well.

row.basis: highway; walkers do not go astray
row.note: The Way of Holiness is a highway on which even inexperienced walkers do not go astray; it brings bodily frailty and a protected route into one prophetic scene.

row.basis: this is the way; right or left
row.note: A voice tells the traveler, This is the way, walk in it, when turning right or left; it answers the commentary's swaying walker with directional guidance.

row.basis: straight path without stumbling
row.note: God leads the returning people by watercourses on a straight path where they will not stumble; this is an unusually close pairing of divine leading, straightness, and safe feet.

row.basis: leading the blind; rough ground level
row.note: God leads blind people on an unknown way and makes rough places level; it extends the source's guide beyond a front-runner to aid for those unable to navigate alone.

row.basis: continuous guidance; strengthened body
row.note: The LORD continually guides, satisfies need in parched places, and makes the bones strong; this joins the commentary's need, support, and restored movement.

row.basis: making paths straight
row.note: Acknowledging God results in paths made straight; it is a concise wisdom analogue to the communal petition for the straight path.

row.basis: led in paths of uprightness
row.note: The teacher leads the pupil in the way of wisdom and paths of uprightness; it joins route-guidance to the moral and bodily verticality heard in mustaqim.

row.basis: unhampered steps; no stumble in running
row.note: The instructed walker has unhampered steps and does not stumble even when running; it gives a contrast to the source's impaired gait and its recovery.

row.basis: do not turn right or left
row.note: The command not to swerve right or left and to keep the foot from evil makes the commentary's literal side-to-side wavering an ethical path image.

row.basis: hasty feet lose the way
row.note: The proverb says that one who hastens with the feet misses the way; it supplies a wisdom contrast to the source's calm, non-panicked good walking.

row.basis: pillar leading the way
row.note: The LORD goes before Israel in a pillar to lead the way; it brings together the commentary's guide, road, and qiyam-as-pillar imagery.

row.basis: bind injured; strengthen weak
row.note: The shepherd seeks the lost, binds the injured, and strengthens the weak; it converts the source's individual supporting act into pastoral responsibility.

row.basis: 'ayn B007/B011; upheld servant
row.note: The source labels na'budu with the 'ayn-b-d root; Isaiah calls the chosen eved God's servant and says God upholds him, a cognate service-and-support pairing.

row.basis: m-l-k B001/B005; king who saves
row.note: The source labels malik with m-l-k; Isaiah's melek is the cognate king term and names the LORD as king who saves us, tying sovereignty to needed deliverance.

row.basis: help the weak against the mighty
row.note: Asa asks God to help the powerless against the mighty because none is like God in helping; this makes the source's request for aid an explicit prayer from weakness.

row.basis: servants' eyes toward a master's hand
row.note: The psalm likens its dependence on the LORD's mercy to servants watching their master's hand; it gives the juxtaposition of na'budu and nasta'inu a relational image.

row.basis: one falls; companion lifts
row.note: When one person falls, the other lifts the companion; it supplies the social logic behind the source's weak traveler being held rather than left alone.

row.basis: traveler seeks someone who knows the road
row.note: Raphael says he knows the roads to Media and has traveled them often; Tobias's journey turns the request for guidance into finding a competent companion.

row.basis: Wisdom guides on straight paths
row.note: Wisdom guides the fleeing righteous person on straight paths; this is a Jewish-scriptural personification of the guidance sought in ihdina.

row.basis: level ground so Israel walks safely
row.note: God levels mountains and fills valleys so Israel may walk safely; it develops the source's straightened route as a bodily safe passage.

row.basis: traveler's prayer for leading and safe arrival
row.note: The Tefillat ha-Derekh asks God to lead, guide, sustain, and bring the traveler to the destination in peace; it is a direct Jewish liturgical analogue to asking aid and a way.

row.basis: rider on a donkey directs the heart
row.note: The mishnah treats a rider on a donkey who cannot dismount for prayer and directs the heart toward the sanctuary; it keeps the source's mount-bound traveler inside a disciplined prayer practice.

row.basis: drooping hands; weak knees
row.note: The exhortation to lift drooping hands and strengthen weak knees takes up the same weakened limbs that the commentary imagines before aid.

row.basis: straight paths for feet; lame healed
row.note: Straight paths are to be made for the feet so that the lame may be healed rather than dislocated; it is one of the closest Christian fusions of straight path, gait, and restoration.

row.basis: right hand raises; feet strengthened
row.note: Peter takes the lame man by the right hand and raises him, and his feet and ankles become strong; it gives the source's hand-held help a concrete upright result.

row.basis: leaps up, stands, and walks
row.note: The healed man leaps up, stands, and walks; this provides the full bodily sequence that the commentary reads into aid followed by upright movement.

row.basis: bent over; unable to straighten
row.note: The woman's disabling spirit leaves her bent and unable to straighten; it supplies an exact counter-image to the upright mustaqim walker.

row.basis: made straight after Jesus' touch
row.note: After Jesus lays hands on her, the woman is immediately made straight; the touch makes aid visibly become upright posture.

row.basis: no one to help the disabled man
row.note: The disabled man says he has no person to put him into the pool; this sharpens the commentary's premise that a weak traveler cannot manage alone.

row.basis: rise, take up bed, walk
row.note: Jesus commands the man to rise, carry his bed, and walk; it gives the source's requested help its compact standing-and-road outcome.

row.basis: four people carry a paralytic
row.note: Four people carry the paralytic to Jesus; the scene makes communal bodily assistance the condition of bringing an immobilized person forward.

row.basis: rise and go home
row.note: The paralytic is told to rise, take up his mat, and go home; it turns the carried body's recovery into independent walking.

row.basis: stand upright and walk
row.note: Paul commands a man disabled in his feet to stand upright, and he leaps and walks; its wording explicitly joins uprightness to restored motion.

row.basis: injured traveler placed on an animal
row.note: The Samaritan binds an injured traveler's wounds, puts him on his own animal, and brings him to care; it reverses the source's failed mount into a means of carrying the weak.

row.basis: weary and burdened invited to rest
row.note: Jesus invites the weary and burdened to come for rest; it gives the commentary's exhausted traveler a direct address and relief.

row.basis: gentle yoke and rest for souls
row.note: Taking Jesus' gentle yoke brings rest; it supplies a Christian image of a burden that supports rather than overwhelms the weak walker.

row.basis: sinking walker cries for rescue
row.note: Peter begins to sink while walking and cries, Lord, save me; the scene makes the commentary's helpless request arise at a literal failure of footing.

row.basis: Jesus immediately takes a hand
row.note: Jesus immediately reaches out and takes the sinking man's hand; it is a direct one-handed counterpart to the source's supported traveler.

row.basis: Spirit helps weakness in prayer
row.note: The Spirit helps human weakness when people do not know how to pray; it applies requested divine aid to the very act of supplication.

row.basis: throne of grace; timely help
row.note: Approaching the throne yields mercy and grace for timely help; it sets the source's plea for aid before a sovereign, as malik frames the petition.

row.basis: strong bear the weak's frailties
row.note: The strong are obliged to bear the frailties of the weak; it states the communal duty implicit in the commentary's two supporting companions.

row.basis: bear one another's burdens
row.note: Bearing one another's burdens makes bodily support an ethic of communal walking rather than an isolated rescue.

row.basis: help the weak; be patient
row.note: The community is told to help the weak and be patient with all; it pairs the source's assistance with the unhurried disposition of good walking.

row.basis: help the weak
row.note: The elders are reminded that one must help the weak; this concise imperative provides a communal form of the source's avn, help.

row.basis: guide feet into the way of peace
row.note: The dawn from on high guides feet into the way of peace; it closely matches ihdina as guidance enacted at the feet.

row.basis: make paths straight
row.note: John's proclamation uses Isaiah's command to make the Lord's paths straight; it gives the straight-path language a preparatory and eschatological Christian setting.

row.basis: How can I unless someone guides me?
row.note: The Ethiopian traveler asks how he can understand unless someone guides him and invites Philip into the chariot; it turns guidance into companioned instruction on a journey.

row.basis: prayer raises the sick
row.note: The prayer of faith saves the sick and the Lord raises the person up; it joins prayer for aid to physical recovery and rising.

row.basis: the Lord stood by and strengthened me
row.note: The Lord stands by Paul and strengthens him in abandonment; it gives the commentary's needed support a personal divine companion.

row.basis: rooted, built up, established
row.note: Believers are rooted, built up, and established in faith; it brings together the commentary's tree-on-roots and stable-wall images.

row.basis: body held together by supporting joints
row.note: The whole body is joined and held together through every supporting joint; it translates the commentary's body-support image into reciprocal communal cohesion.

row.basis: house does not fall because founded on rock
row.note: The house withstands storm because it has a rock foundation; it gives the source's wall and structural support imagery an ethical architectural counterpart.

row.basis: kept from stumbling and made to stand
row.note: God is able to keep believers from stumbling and make them stand; it compresses the source's protected gait and upright result into doxology.

row.basis: tree with many roots resists wind
row.note: Rabbi Eleazar ben Azariah compares deeds exceeding wisdom to a tree with many roots that storms cannot uproot; it interprets rootedness as the moral stability behind the source's standing tree.

row.basis: sons of righteousness walk in paths of light
row.note: The Community Rule places the sons of righteousness under the Prince of Lights and says they walk in paths of light; it gives the requested right way an angelic and communal Second Temple framing.

row.basis: walking after God means acts of care
row.note: The talmudic reading of walking after God turns the command into clothing, visiting, comforting, and burying the vulnerable; it makes walking with God inseparable from supporting the weak.

row.basis: foot-protection promise used as temptation
row.note: The tempter cites angelic foot-protection to urge Jesus to leap; beside the source's needy petition, it raises the distinct question of asking for aid versus demanding a proof of it.

row.basis: do not test God
row.note: Jesus answers the appeal to protection by forbidding the testing of God; it supplies the interpretive boundary for the preceding scene's use of divine support.

row.basis: Jesus identifies himself as the way
row.note: Where the source has a community ask God to guide it on a straight path, John identifies Jesus himself as the way to the Father; the contrast is a substantive Christological recasting of path language.

row.basis: Spirit guides into all truth
row.note: The Spirit of truth guides disciples into all truth; it extends the source's request for a guide from physical route-finding to discernment.

row.basis: Jesus joins travelers on the road
row.note: Jesus draws near and travels with the disoriented disciples to Emmaus; it makes guidance take the form of a companion sharing the road.

row.basis: Lamb shepherds and guides to waters
row.note: The Lamb shepherds the afflicted and guides them to springs of life-giving water; it combines leadership, relief, and a destination for the needy traveler.

row.basis: pillar and foundation of truth
row.note: The church is called the pillar and foundation of truth; it gives the commentary's qiyam-as-pillar image an ecclesial structural use.

row.basis: power perfected in weakness
row.note: Christ's power is made perfect in weakness; it supplies a theological reading in which the source's weakness remains the place where enabling aid is displayed.

row.basis: apart from me you can do nothing
row.note: Branches can bear fruit only by remaining in the vine, and apart from Christ disciples can do nothing; it gives the source's inability to proceed alone an organic image of dependence.

row.basis: the Way of Life and the Way of Death
row.note: The Didache opens with the Way of Life and the Way of Death; it supplies an early Christian ethical development of the path metaphor, though its two-way scheme goes beyond this section's single petition.

row.basis: we seek from God a straight way
row.note: Ezra proclaims a fast so the traveling community may seek from God a straight way for themselves, their children, and their goods; it closely joins communal petition, dependence, and the requested road.

row.basis: God's hand helps travelers on the road
row.note: Ezra contrasts royal military help with God's favorable hand on those who seek him while facing enemies on the way; it gives nasta'inu a travel-specific account of divine aid.

row.basis: fasting and entreating God for the journey
row.note: The community fasts and entreats God for the safe journey, and God answers; it supplies a concrete liturgical continuation of asking help before setting out.

row.basis: donkey collapsed under a burden
row.note: The law requires helping even an enemy's donkey when it lies under its load; it gives the commentary's exhausted mount an ethical command not to leave it stranded.

row.basis: fallen donkey on the road; lift it up
row.note: The law forbids ignoring a fellow Israelite's fallen donkey on the road and requires raising it with the owner; it directly answers the source's stopped mount with shared assistance.

row.basis: traveler asks guarding, food, and clothing
row.note: Jacob asks that God be with him, guard him on the way, and provide bread and clothing; it gives the vulnerable traveler a prayer for both protection and material support.

row.basis: guide on a way not traveled before
row.note: The ark goes ahead so Israel will know the way to go because it has not passed that way before; it is a precise narrative of a guide for people unable to orient themselves alone.

row.basis: 'ayn-b-d B007/B011; walk all God's ways
row.note: Deuteronomy couples walking in all God's ways with serving God from the whole heart; Hebrew avad is cognate with the source label for na'budu and preserves its worship-and-way sequence.

row.basis: 'ayn-b-d B007/B011; service and bodily healing
row.note: Israel is to serve God, who blesses bread and water and removes sickness; the Hebrew avad cognate places service beside the bodily strengthening the commentary associates with aid.

row.basis: mercy leads and guides to water
row.note: The hungry and thirsty are protected from scorching because the merciful one leads and guides them to springs; it gives the source's needy traveler both relief and a destination.

row.basis: build up the way; remove obstruction
row.note: God commands that a road be built and every obstruction removed from the people's way; it turns the commentary's support and wall imagery into preparation for safe passage.

row.basis: carry, bear, and save through frailty
row.note: God promises to carry and bear people even into old age and gray hair; it supplies a sustained divine counterpart to the source's body that needs to be held up.

row.basis: assemble the lame and afflicted
row.note: God will gather the lame, the outcast, and those afflicted; it makes the physically impaired people in the source an object of restoration rather than abandonment.

row.basis: lame remnant made a strong nation
row.note: The lame are made a remnant and the outcast a strong nation; this gives the commentary's movement from weakness to solidity a collective prophetic form.

row.basis: save the lame and gather the outcast
row.note: God promises to save the lame and gather the outcast; it gives direct prophetic content to aid for those whose movement and social standing are impaired.

row.basis: spirit sets the hearer on his feet
row.note: The spirit enters Ezekiel and sets him on his feet while God speaks; it is a direct scene in which enabling presence produces upright posture.

row.basis: touch that strengthens a weakened body
row.note: A humanlike figure touches the overwhelmed Daniel and strengthens him; this supplies a bodily counterpart to the source's aid turning weakness into steadiness.

row.basis: peace and strength received after speech
row.note: The messenger says peace and be strong, and Daniel reports being strengthened; it adds spoken reassurance to the commentary's supported, non-panicked recovery.

row.basis: feet made like a deer's; secure heights
row.note: God gives the speaker agile feet and sets him securely on heights; it reframes restored walking as divinely given bodily surety.

row.basis: right hand supports the speaker
row.note: God's right hand supports the speaker; it is a close biblical counterpart to the commentary's claim that aid is a support under a vulnerable person.

row.basis: broad footing; ankles do not slip
row.note: God makes room for the speaker's steps so the ankles do not give way; it specifies secure footing as the result of help.

row.basis: God gives strength and sure feet
row.note: God is the speaker's strength, makes the feet like a deer's, and enables walking on heights; it closely combines strength, gait, and difficult terrain.

row.basis: level path of the righteous
row.note: The path of the righteous is level because God makes it level; it supplies a Hebrew formulation in which moral rightness and an even route converge.

row.basis: God leads in the way one should go
row.note: God teaches what is beneficial and leads the people in the way they should go; it is a direct prophetic response to the plea ihdina.

row.basis: walk securely; foot does not stumble
row.note: The wise person walks securely and does not stumble; it gives the commentary's restored gait a wisdom counterpart.

row.basis: lead me in the path of commandments
row.note: The psalmist asks to be led in the path of God's commandments; this is a direct first-person prayer for guidance alongside ihdina.

row.basis: establish my steps in your word
row.note: The psalmist asks God to establish the steps in the divine word; it joins the source's standing and walking imagery to a petition for firm footing.

row.basis: Wisdom helps those who seek her
row.note: Wisdom instructs her children and gives help to those who seek her; it explicitly joins sought assistance to instruction and guidance.

row.basis: pray that the Most High direct your way
row.note: The sage tells the reader to pray that the Most High direct the way in truth; it is a close Jewish wisdom analogue to asking for the straight path.

row.basis: Moses' raised hands interpreted as dependence
row.note: The talmudic reading of Exodus 17 says Moses' hands did not themselves win the battle; Israel prevailed when they turned their hearts upward, turning bodily support into worshipful dependence.

row.basis: supports used to undergird a ship
row.note: In a storm the sailors use supports to undergird their ship; this gives the commentary's avn as what one relies on a literal structural and travel-related enactment.

row.basis: worship while leaning on a staff
row.note: Jacob worships while leaning on the top of his staff; it brings worship, bodily support, and the vulnerable traveler's staff into a single Christian-scriptural image.

row.basis: taken by hand, raised, then serves
row.note: Jesus takes the fevered woman by the hand and raises her, after which she serves; the scene sequences aid, upright recovery, and service like the source's linked worship and help.

row.basis: Jesus takes a hand, raises, and the boy stands
row.note: Jesus takes the boy's hand, raises him, and he stands; it closely parallels the source's hand-supported body becoming upright.

row.basis: traveler left half dead on the road
row.note: The traveler falls among robbers and is left half dead; this supplies the vulnerable roadside condition to which the Samaritan's assistance in the existing scene responds.

row.basis: lost sheep carried on shoulders
row.note: The shepherd places the found sheep on his shoulders; it offers a pastoral image of carrying one unable to return by its own strength.

row.basis: come over and help us
row.note: A Macedonian man asks Paul to cross over and help them; the request makes aid both communal and tied to a journey across a boundary.

row.basis: servant made to stand by the Lord
row.note: The servant stands or falls before the master, yet the Lord is able to make the servant stand; it brings service, dependence, and uprightness into one statement.

row.basis: do not place a stumbling block before the blind
row.note: The law prohibits placing a stumbling block before the blind; it gives the source's guided weak traveler a negative ethical counterpart, removing what causes a fall.

row.basis: curse on making a blind person stray
row.note: The curse falls on one who makes a blind person wander off the road; it casts the source's needed guidance as a communal obligation not to misdirect the vulnerable.

row.basis: communal petition for protection from testing
row.note: The plural prayer asks not to be brought into testing and to be delivered from evil; it forms a Christian liturgical companion to the communal request for guided protection.

row.basis: do not put obstacle in a brother's way
row.note: Believers are told not to put a stumbling block or obstacle in another's way; it turns the source's safe path into a responsibility toward a fellow walker.

row.basis: weaker members of the body are indispensable
row.note: The body's apparently weaker members are indispensable; it deepens the commentary's body-and-support image by making weakness a condition for mutual care.

row.basis: able to help those being tested
row.note: Because Jesus suffered when tested, he is able to help those tested; it offers a Christological account of help arising from shared vulnerability.

row.basis: restore, strengthen, establish, and found
row.note: God restores, strengthens, establishes, and founds believers after suffering; the cluster gives the source's wall, pillar, and uprightness images a Christian form.

row.basis: lordly service enacted by washing feet
row.note: Jesus the Lord washes disciples' feet and commands reciprocal service; it joins the source's worship-and-help pair to a concrete care for the body's walking members.

row.basis: strength for endurance and patience
row.note: Believers are strengthened with power for endurance and patience; it gives the source's aided, unhurried walking an inward ethical correlate.

row.basis: ask God to give what God commands
row.note: Augustine asks God to give what God commands before commanding what God wills; it is a classic Christian interpretation of obedience as requiring the very aid the worshiper petitions for.

row.basis: an angel strengthens Jesus in prayer
row.note: The angel strengthens Jesus during prayer, closely joining supplication and enabling aid; the verses are absent from some early witnesses, so this candidate requires textual verification.
